title: In-situ Electric-Field-Assisted Growth of GaAs Nanowires
content: The vapor-liquid-solid (VLS) method for the growth of semiconductor wires was introduced by Wagner and Ellis in the 1960s [1]. Since then, intensive research has been carried out on the engineering of the growth of nanowires, due to their promising applications in nanotechnology [2]. A critical aspect for developing nanowire-based devices is the precise control of growth rates, which is set by various factors, in particular temperature and vapor fluxes. However, the interplay between nanowire size, spatial distribution, and these external conditions can make control challenging. For instance, adjustments in growth conditions, such as increasing temperature, may even yield divergent effects on growth rates, depending on the other growth parameters. Previous study [3] has demonstrated that use of electric field (E-field) can alter the shape of the liquid droplet seating on the tip of Au-catalyzed Si nanowires. Yet, a fundamental question persists: how can an E-field be harnessed to directly regulate atomic-scale growth dynamics, rather than merely altering droplet morphology?
